```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE)
options(width = 90)
```

## Purpose and output

This internal preparation report documents how the published web text of *Value
pluralism in research integrity* is acquired for the Chapter 17 word-search
activity. It replaces the earlier PDF-extraction workflow in this copy of the
report. The original article wording, punctuation, and genuine hyphens are
preserved; the code does not paraphrase the article.

This workflow creates **paragraph-sized, natural text passages** and saves the
plain character vector as `Science_Values.rds` in the chapter's `data` folder.
Each paragraph, list item, note, reference, or identification record becomes one
passage. Headings are attached to the next passage in source order, once each.
The article is not split into sentences or flattened into one large string.

The structured extraction is retained in memory for checking how each passage
relates to the web page. Running the complete report replaces the existing
`Science_Values.rds` with the new Peels and colleagues text. Chapter editing and
book publication remain separate tasks.

The retained material includes article identification, the abstract and main
text, notes, references, acknowledgements, funding, the contribution statement,
ethics declarations, the publisher's note, and the article's rights notice.
Author affiliations, postal and email addresses, correspondence details, site
navigation, sharing tools, and reference-search buttons are excluded.

## Source and permission evidence

Peels, Rik, Jeroen de Ridder, Tamarinde Haven, and Lex Bouter. (2019).
"Value pluralism in research integrity." *Research Integrity and Peer Review*,
4, Article 18. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s41073-019-0076-4>.

The source is the publisher's version of record, published on 22 August 2019:
<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41073-019-0076-4>.

The publisher's [Rights and permissions
notice](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41073-019-0076-4#rightslink)
identifies the article as **Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
(CC BY 4.0)**. This is explicit reuse evidence, rather than an inference from
free access. The [license](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
permits redistribution and adaptation, including commercial reuse, subject to
its terms. Credit the authors and source, retain supplied notices, link to the
license, and identify changes. The code below retains the article's actual
notice together with its text and records the preparation changes.

The notice also mentions CC0 for data made available in the article. That
statement does not replace the CC BY license for the article prose. Attributed
quotations from research codes are retained with their credits. Their underlying
source licenses have not been independently verified by this workflow; any
specific third-party exclusions need review before final redistribution.

## 1. Check the required tools

`rvest` reads the HTML elements of a web page, and `xml2` lets us inspect their
structure. `stringr` checks the chapter's word searches, and `knitr` displays
review tables in the report. Install missing packages
once, outside the routine extraction. This report does not install anything
automatically.

```{r install-once, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("rvest", "xml2", "stringr", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
```

The check below stops with a clear message if a required package is unavailable.

```{r check-packages}
required_packages <- c("rvest", "xml2", "stringr", "knitr", "rmarkdown")
available <- vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
if (!all(available)) {
  stop("Install the missing packages first: ",
       paste(required_packages[!available], collapse = ", "))
}
```

## 2. Read the publisher's web text

Normally, the report reads directly from the article URL and requires an internet
connection. The optional `source_html` parameter can instead point to a locally
saved copy of that same HTML page for checking. A local copy must still pass the
source and license checks below. The run time is an extraction time, not a claim
about when a local copy was originally downloaded.

```{r read-web-text}
article_url <- "https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41073-019-0076-4"
expected_doi <- "10.1186/s41073-019-0076-4"
# Knit supplies params; running chunks interactively can use the live-page default.
source_html <- if (exists("params")) params$source_html else NULL
source_input <- if (is.null(source_html)) article_url else source_html

article_page <- xml2::read_html(source_input)
extracted_at <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z", tz = "America/Boise")
source_mode <- if (is.null(source_html)) "Live publisher page" else "Local HTML copy"

data.frame(source = source_mode, input = source_input, extraction_time = extracted_at)
```

## 3. Read and verify the article identification

The page includes citation metadata intended to identify the article. We read
only the named fields needed here, rather than copying all metadata, which also
contains author contact details. The online publication date is used because
the separate `citation_publication_date` field describes the journal issue date.

```{r read-identification}
meta_value <- function(name) {
  rvest::html_elements(article_page, paste0("meta[name='", name, "']")) |>
    rvest::html_attr("content")
}

article_title <- meta_value("citation_title")
author_names <- sub("^([^,]+), (.*)$", "\\2 \\1", meta_value("citation_author"))
publication_date <- as.Date(meta_value("citation_online_date"), format = "%Y/%m/%d")
journal <- meta_value("citation_journal_title")
volume <- meta_value("citation_volume")
article_number <- meta_value("citation_firstpage")
doi <- meta_value("citation_doi")
copyright_notice <- meta_value("dc.rights")

stopifnot(
  identical(article_title, "Value pluralism in research integrity"),
  identical(doi, expected_doi),
  identical(author_names, c("Rik Peels", "Jeroen de Ridder", "Tamarinde Haven", "Lex Bouter")),
  identical(as.character(publication_date), "2019-08-22"),
  length(copyright_notice) == 1L, nzchar(copyright_notice)
)
```

The license link is checked in the article's own rights section. This check would
fail rather than accepting a different license or a page without that
notice.

```{r verify-license}
license_link <- rvest::html_elements(
  article_page,
  "section[data-title='Rights and permissions'] a[rel='license'][href*='/licenses/by/4.0']"
)
license_url <- rvest::html_attr(license_link, "href")
stopifnot(length(license_url) == 1L,
          grepl("^https?://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4[.]0/?$", license_url))

citation <- paste0(
  paste(author_names, collapse = "; "), ". (", format(publication_date, "%Y"), "). ",
  article_title, ". ", journal, ", ", volume, ", Article ", article_number,
  ". https://doi.org/", doi
)
```

## 4. Select article content and remove web controls

An explicit list of article sections keeps navigation and contact information
out of the extraction. It also makes the content boundary visible for review.
The contribution statement is selected separately because it shares a section
with author addresses and correspondence information.

```{r select-sections}
keep_sections <- c(
  "Abstract", "Introduction", "Background",
  "Metaphysical pluralism: values, norms, and virtues",
  "Axiological pluralism: five categories of normativity",
  "Axiological pluralism 1: Incommensurable norms from different categories",
  "Axiological pluralism 2: Conflicting norms from the same category",
  "Overcoming pluralism?", "Conclusions", "Availability of data and materials",
  "Notes", "References", "Acknowledgements", "Funding",
  "Ethics declarations", "Additional information", "Rights and permissions"
)

page_sections <- rvest::html_elements(article_page, "article section[data-title]")
stopifnot(all(keep_sections %in% rvest::html_attr(page_sections, "data-title")))
stopifnot(length(rvest::html_elements(article_page, "#contributions")) == 1L)
```

The reference list has separate Google Scholar, article-search, and citation
download controls. The rights section also has a reprint-order link. These are removed from
the working HTML; reference citations and the rights notice remain intact.
Footnote callouts are displayed as `[Note n]` so they do not run into adjacent
words. Their link targets are preserved.

```{r remove-controls}
web_controls <- rvest::html_elements(
  article_page,
  ".c-article-references__links, .c-article-references__download, .c-article-rights"
)
xml2::xml_remove(web_controls)

note_links <- rvest::html_elements(article_page, "sup a[href^='#Fn']")
for (node in note_links) {
  note_number <- sub("#Fn", "", rvest::html_attr(node, "href"), fixed = TRUE)
  # Remove both the hidden label span and the original numeric text first.
  xml2::xml_remove(xml2::xml_contents(node))
  xml2::xml_text(node) <- paste0(" [Note ", note_number, "]")
}
```

## 5. Retain the existing HTML blocks in source order

The selection below keeps headings, paragraphs, and complete list items. A
paragraph inside a selected list item is not selected again, so list text is
not duplicated. Notes and references remain list items at this stage.

```{r select-blocks}
section_rule <- paste0("@data-title='", keep_sections, "'", collapse = " or ")
block_rule <- paste(
  "self::h2 or self::h3 or self::h4 or self::h5 or self::h6 or self::p or self::li"
)
block_xpath <- paste0(
  "//article//section[", section_rule, "]//*[", block_rule, "][not(ancestor::li)]",
  " | //article//h3[@id='contributions']",
  " | //article//h3[@id='contributions']/following-sibling::p[1]"
)
block_nodes <- xml2::xml_find_all(article_page, block_xpath)
stopifnot(length(block_nodes) > 0L)
```

`html_text2()` reads text in a browser-like way, retaining breaks within each
block. It normalizes HTML display whitespace and nonbreaking spaces. We do not
flatten the whole article, remove ordinary hyphens, or split sentences. Section
names and HTML identifiers provide a way back to the source.

```{r record-blocks}
sections <- vapply(block_nodes, function(node) {
  xml2::xml_find_first(node, "ancestor::section[@data-title][1]") |>
    rvest::html_attr("data-title")
}, character(1))

block_text <- rvest::html_text2(block_nodes)
elements <- xml2::xml_name(block_nodes)
source_ids <- rvest::html_attr(block_nodes, "id")
is_reference <- sections == "References" & elements == "li"
source_ids[is_reference] <- vapply(block_nodes[is_reference], function(node) {
  rvest::html_element(node, ".c-article-references__text") |> rvest::html_attr("id")
}, character(1))
source_ids[is.na(source_ids)] <- ""

block_kind <- ifelse(grepl("^h[2-6]$", elements), "heading",
                     ifelse(elements == "li", "list_item", "paragraph"))
block_kind[sections == "Notes" & elements == "li"] <- "note"
block_kind[is_reference] <- "reference"
```

List labels are sometimes supplied through HTML attributes or a separate span,
rather than through paragraph text. We keep those labels in their own column.
This preserves note and reference numbering, bullets, and the article's numbered
categories for the passage assembly below.
Some custom numbers already occur in `text` as well as in `list_label`; later
assembly must check for an existing label rather than adding it twice.

```{r retain-list-labels}
list_types <- vapply(block_nodes, function(node) {
  if (xml2::xml_name(node) == "li") xml2::xml_name(xml2::xml_parent(node)) else ""
}, character(1))

list_labels <- vapply(block_nodes, function(node) {
  if (xml2::xml_name(node) != "li") return("")
  counter <- rvest::html_attr(node, "data-counter")
  if (!is.na(counter)) return(counter)
  custom <- rvest::html_element(node, ".u-custom-list-number") |> rvest::html_text2()
  if (!is.na(custom)) return(custom)
  if (xml2::xml_name(xml2::xml_parent(node)) == "ul") return("-")
  paste0(length(xml2::xml_find_all(node, "preceding-sibling::li")) + 1L, ".")
}, character(1))

article_blocks <- data.frame(
  section = sections, kind = block_kind, element = elements,
  source_id = source_ids, list_type = list_types, list_label = list_labels,
  text = block_text, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

The heading path records the section and subsection that contain each block.
Repeated text is not deleted merely because the same wording appears elsewhere;
for example, separate declarations may legitimately both say "Not applicable."

```{r retain-heading-paths}
heading_stack <- rep("", 6L)
previous_section <- ""
article_blocks$section_path <- ""
for (i in seq_len(nrow(article_blocks))) {
  if (article_blocks$section[i] != previous_section) {
    heading_stack[] <- ""
    heading_stack[2] <- article_blocks$section[i]
  }
  if (article_blocks$kind[i] == "heading") {
    level <- as.integer(sub("h", "", article_blocks$element[i], fixed = TRUE))
    heading_stack[level:6L] <- ""
    heading_stack[level] <- article_blocks$text[i]
  }
  article_blocks$section_path[i] <- paste(heading_stack[nzchar(heading_stack)], collapse = " > ")
  previous_section <- article_blocks$section[i]
}
```

## 6. Keep identification and attribution with the extracted material

These explicitly labeled records place the title, all four authors, publication
date, full citation, source URL, copyright, license, and preparation note in the
same structure as the article text. They are included in the saved searchable
text, rather than being left only in this report.
The publisher's complete rights notice is also retained in its original section.

```{r add-identification}
preparation_note <- paste(
  "Extracted from publisher HTML for an instructional text-search activity.",
  "Article identification and preparation records were added; web controls and",
  "author contact/affiliation details were excluded. HTML display whitespace was",
  "normalized and footnote callouts displayed as [Note n]. Natural paragraphs,",
  "list items, notes, references, and identification records form the passages.",
  "Headings are attached once to the next passage; list numbering and the rights",
  "notice are retained. Word counts describe the supplied text, including its metadata."
)

identification <- data.frame(
  label = c("Title", "Authors", "Published", "Citation", "Source", "Copyright",
            "License", "License URL", "Extraction time", "Preparation note"),
  value = c(article_title, paste(author_names, collapse = "; "),
            as.character(publication_date), citation, article_url, copyright_notice,
            "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)",
            license_url, extracted_at, preparation_note),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

identification_blocks <- data.frame(
  section = "Article identification", kind = "metadata", element = "metadata",
  source_id = "", list_type = "", list_label = "",
  text = paste0(identification$label, ": ", identification$value),
  section_path = "Article identification", stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

Science_Values_web <- rbind(identification_blocks, article_blocks)
Science_Values_web$block_id <- seq_len(nrow(Science_Values_web))
Science_Values_web <- Science_Values_web[, c("block_id", "section", "section_path",
  "kind", "element", "source_id", "list_type", "list_label", "text")]

knitr::kable(identification, caption = "Identification retained with the article text")
```

## 7. Retain citation and note links for traceability

Text extraction by itself does not retain hyperlink destinations. This companion
table associates each retained article link with its block. Internal note and
reference links are converted to complete publisher URLs. Link labels are not
added to the text a second time. No linked document is downloaded.

```{r retain-links}
link_rows <- lapply(seq_along(block_nodes), function(i) {
  links <- rvest::html_elements(block_nodes[[i]], "a[href]")
  if (length(links) == 0L) return(NULL)
  href <- rvest::html_attr(links, "href")
  keep <- !grepl("^mailto:", href, ignore.case = TRUE)
  data.frame(
    block_id = rep(i + nrow(identification_blocks), sum(keep)),
    label = rvest::html_text2(links)[keep],
    url = xml2::url_absolute(href[keep], article_url), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
Science_Values_links <- do.call(rbind, link_rows)
stopifnot(!is.null(Science_Values_links), nrow(Science_Values_links) > 0L)
```

## 8. Check the extracted source structure

These checks concern this specific published article. Its 17 notes and 50
references provide useful completeness checks. They are not keyword counts.
The checks also confirm that contact information and reference-search controls
have not entered the retained text. If the publisher changes the page structure,
a failed check calls for inspection rather than producing a new file.

```{r check-extraction}
checks <- c(
  all_blocks_have_text = all(!is.na(Science_Values_web$text) & nzchar(trimws(Science_Values_web$text))),
  all_selected_sections_present = all(keep_sections %in% Science_Values_web$section),
  contributions_retained = "contributions" %in% Science_Values_web$source_id,
  seventeen_notes_retained = sum(Science_Values_web$kind == "note") == 17L,
  fifty_references_retained = sum(Science_Values_web$kind == "reference") == 50L,
  final_reference_retained = "ref-CR50" %in% Science_Values_web$source_id,
  genuine_hyphen_retained = any(grepl("open-mindedness", article_blocks$text, fixed = TRUE)),
  no_duplicated_note_numbers = !any(vapply(seq_len(17L), function(n) {
    any(grepl(paste0("[Note ", n, "]", n), Science_Values_web$text, fixed = TRUE))
  }, logical(1))),
  no_email_addresses = !any(grepl("[[:alnum:]._%+-]+@[[:alnum:].-]+\\.[[:alpha:]]{2,}", Science_Values_web$text)),
  no_postal_affiliations = !any(grepl("De Boelelaan", Science_Values_web$text, fixed = TRUE)),
  no_correspondence_details = !any(grepl("Correspondence to", Science_Values_web$text, fixed = TRUE)),
  no_reference_search_buttons = !any(grepl("Google Scholar", Science_Values_web$text, fixed = TRUE)),
  no_reference_download_control = !any(grepl("Download references", Science_Values_web$text, fixed = TRUE)),
  no_reprint_order_link = !any(grepl("Reprints and permissions", Science_Values_web$text, fixed = TRUE))
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(check = names(checks), passed = unname(checks)))
stopifnot(all(checks))
```

The section inventory shows what was retained. It counts source blocks, which
should not yet be interpreted as counts of student search passages.

```{r inspect-inventory}
section_order <- unique(Science_Values_web$section)
inventory <- data.frame(
  section = section_order,
  source_blocks = vapply(section_order, function(s) sum(Science_Values_web$section == s), integer(1))
)
knitr::kable(inventory, caption = "Retained source structure")
```

The short preview makes headings, list labels, a note, a reference, and the rights
notice easy to locate. Preview text is shortened for display only; the extraction
object retains the complete text of every selected block.

```{r inspect-preview}
preview_rows <- unique(c(
  which(Science_Values_web$kind == "heading")[1:2],
  which(Science_Values_web$kind == "list_item")[1],
  which(Science_Values_web$kind == "note")[1],
  which(Science_Values_web$kind == "reference")[1],
  which(Science_Values_web$section == "Rights and permissions" &
          Science_Values_web$kind == "paragraph")[1]
))
preview <- Science_Values_web[preview_rows, c("block_id", "section_path", "kind", "list_label", "text")]
preview$text <- paste0(substr(preview$text, 1, 140), ifelse(nchar(preview$text) > 140, "...", ""))
knitr::kable(preview, caption = "Preview only: source text is not truncated in the extraction")
```

## 9. Prepare paragraph-sized passages and list labels

Each existing paragraph or list item remains intact. Individual notes,
references, and identification records also remain separate entries. Only
whitespace inside a block is collapsed; genuine hyphens, punctuation, citations,
and note callouts remain. Headings will be attached in the next step.

```{r prepare-passage-text}
passage_rows <- which(Science_Values_web$kind != "heading")
passage_sources <- Science_Values_web[passage_rows, ]
passage_text <- stringr::str_squish(passage_sources$text)
```

Some list numbers are already in the text, while other numbers and bullets were
supplied only by HTML. The helper checks the literal label and the following
space, so that a label such as `1.` is not confused with a value such as `1.5`.
Missing labels are added once; existing labels are left in place.

```{r assemble-list-labels}
has_list_label <- function(text, label) {
  if (!nzchar(label) || !startsWith(text, label)) return(FALSE)
  remainder <- substring(text, nchar(label) + 1L)
  !nzchar(remainder) || grepl("^[[:space:]]", remainder)
}

for (i in seq_along(passage_text)) {
  label <- passage_sources$list_label[i]
  if (nzchar(label) && !has_list_label(passage_text[i], label)) {
    passage_text[i] <- paste(label, passage_text[i])
  }
}
```

## 10. Attach each heading to its next passage

Headings remain in their original order and appear once, before the next
non-heading block. This avoids isolated heading-only results and avoids
artificially repeating a heading's keywords in every paragraph. Blank lines
separate headings from the paragraph text. A source map records all blocks
included in each passage; it is kept in the report environment rather than
adding attributes to the student's character vector.

```{r assemble-passages}
Science_Values <- character(length(passage_rows))
included_blocks <- vector("list", length(passage_rows))
pending_headings <- character()
pending_ids <- integer()
passage_id <- 0L

for (i in seq_len(nrow(Science_Values_web))) {
  if (Science_Values_web$kind[i] == "heading") {
    pending_headings <- c(pending_headings, Science_Values_web$text[i])
    pending_ids <- c(pending_ids, Science_Values_web$block_id[i])
  } else {
    passage_id <- passage_id + 1L
    Science_Values[passage_id] <- paste(
      c(pending_headings, passage_text[passage_id]), collapse = "\n\n"
    )
    included_blocks[[passage_id]] <- c(pending_ids, Science_Values_web$block_id[i])
    pending_headings <- character()
    pending_ids <- integer()
  }
}
stopifnot(length(pending_headings) == 0L, length(pending_ids) == 0L)
```

The source map gives each saved passage its original section, kind, and source
identifier. The list of block IDs also includes any attached headings. Ordinary
paragraphs do not all have HTML identifiers, so the block IDs provide the
complete mapping even when `source_id` is empty.

```{r map-passages}
passage_map <- data.frame(
  passage_id = seq_along(Science_Values),
  section_path = passage_sources$section_path,
  kind = passage_sources$kind,
  source_id = passage_sources$source_id,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
passage_map$included_block_ids <- included_blocks

mapped_ids <- unlist(included_blocks, use.names = FALSE)
passage_checks <- c(
  character_vector = is.character(Science_Values),
  no_extra_attributes = is.null(attributes(Science_Values)),
  all_passages_nonempty = all(nzchar(trimws(Science_Values))),
  one_passage_per_nonheading_block = length(Science_Values) == length(passage_rows),
  every_source_block_retained_once = identical(sort(mapped_ids), Science_Values_web$block_id),
  no_duplicated_source_blocks = !anyDuplicated(mapped_ids),
  title_retained = any(grepl(article_title, Science_Values, fixed = TRUE)),
  license_url_retained = any(grepl(license_url, Science_Values, fixed = TRUE)),
  final_reference_retained = "ref-CR50" %in% passage_map$source_id
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(check = names(passage_checks), passed = unname(passage_checks)))
stopifnot(all(passage_checks))
```

The composition table distinguishes prose paragraphs from other natural entries.
The total is a count of **supplied-text passages**, including identification,
notes, and references, rather than a count of prose paragraphs alone.

```{r inspect-passage-composition}
composition <- as.data.frame(table(passage_map$kind), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(composition) <- c("passage_kind", "number_of_passages")
knitr::kable(composition, caption = "Composition of the saved character vector")
```

## 11. Check the chapter's searches

These are the chapter's current index words, searched as case-insensitive whole
words. A matching passage and a word occurrence are different measures: a word
can occur several times in one matching passage. Both are shown for review. All
retained text is searched, including identification, headings, notes, references,
and licensing information.

```{r check-keyword-searches}
index_words <- c(
  "values", "norms", "integrity", "ethics", "bias", "trust", "transparency",
  "responsibility", "reproducibility", "evidence", "policy", "funding", "conflict"
)
word_pattern <- function(word) {
  stringr::regex(paste0("\\b", word, "\\b"), ignore_case = TRUE)
}

keyword_review <- data.frame(
  word = index_words,
  matching_passages = vapply(index_words, function(word) {
    sum(stringr::str_detect(Science_Values, word_pattern(word)))
  }, integer(1)),
  total_occurrences = vapply(index_words, function(word) {
    sum(stringr::str_count(Science_Values, word_pattern(word)))
  }, integer(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(keyword_review, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Case-insensitive whole-word searches in the supplied text")
```

The same word-occurrence totals must be obtained from the source blocks and the
assembled passages. This checks that heading attachment and label formatting
have neither duplicated nor lost these words. The worked examples also need a
`trust` result and at least two `transparency` passages. An absent keyword remains
an honest zero; changing passage size cannot create a word that is absent.

```{r compare-source-and-passage-searches}
source_counts <- vapply(index_words, function(word) {
  sum(stringr::str_count(Science_Values_web$text, word_pattern(word)))
}, integer(1))
stopifnot(
  identical(unname(source_counts), keyword_review$total_occurrences),
  keyword_review$matching_passages[keyword_review$word == "trust"] > 0L,
  keyword_review$matching_passages[keyword_review$word == "transparency"] >= 2L
)
```

The following preview retrieves the first `trust` match, just as the chapter
retrieves matching text by index. It shows a complete passage rather than a
shortened table cell. A legitimate zero-result search would instead return no
matching indices.

```{r preview-complete-passage}
trust_indices <- which(stringr::str_detect(Science_Values, word_pattern("trust")))
cat(Science_Values[head(trust_indices, 1L)], sep = "\n")
```

### Additional searches about scientific values

Successful matches should return useful information about scientific values,
rather than merely a frequent word. The following additional terms were checked
against the complete saved text. Counts include any notes or references that
match, so the passages also need to be read before choosing worked examples.

```{r check-scientific-values-words}
values_words <- c("carefulness", "honesty", "privacy", "openness", "humility", "virtues")
values_word_review <- data.frame(
  word = values_words,
  matching_passages = vapply(values_words, function(word) {
    sum(stringr::str_detect(Science_Values, word_pattern(word)))
  }, integer(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(values_word_review, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Additional whole-word searches about scientific values")
```

**Instructional judgment after reading the results:** `carefulness` is a strong
worked example because both matches are explanatory paragraphs. One connects
intellectual virtues with honest reporting and acknowledging limitations. The
other considers a novel research result that may reflect equipment or
programming problems, and whether to publish with qualifications or wait.
`honesty` also finds the connection between values and reporting practices.
`privacy` and `openness` retrieve tensions between sharing knowledge and
protecting people or respecting agreements. `humility` returns one substantive
paragraph about listening to other reasonable viewpoints when values conflict.
`virtues` is useful for broader exploration, but returns more material, including
notes and reference entries.

The two complete `carefulness` passages are displayed below so that the proposed
worked example can be reviewed directly. Wrapping the display does not change
the strings saved in the data file.

```{r preview-carefulness-passages}
carefulness_indices <- which(stringr::str_detect(Science_Values, word_pattern("carefulness")))
stopifnot(length(carefulness_indices) == 2L)
for (i in carefulness_indices) {
  cat("\nPassage ", i, "\n", sep = "")
  cat(strwrap(Science_Values[i], width = 88), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}
```

The current chapter's first two `transparency` hits are a short values list and
an introduction to an example; later hits contain more substantial discussion.
For the editor's handoff, a preview using `carefulness` would return two fuller
discussions without requiring a change to the indexing method. A focused
three-word practice set could use `honesty`, `carefulness`, and `privacy`.

Exact whole-word `bias` and `reproducibility` searches remain zero. A word-family
pattern can instead include `biased` and `biases` using the alternation already
introduced in Chapter 17. `ethics` does return matches, but many are in the
references or declarations, so it is less direct as a worked example about the
article's values argument. The editor should specify the matching rule for the
assignment and use `Science_Values` consistently where the chapter currently
also refers to `Science_vec`.

## 12. Save the data file in the chapter's data folder

The normal destination is `chapters/07-thoroughness/data/Science_Values.rds`
inside the OER repository. The code finds the repository from the report's
location, or from the working directory when chunks are run interactively. It
does not depend on Lorraine's home-directory path. If neither location is within
the OER project, open that project before running these chunks.

The optional `data_dir` parameter supplies a different existing folder for a
temporary validation run. It is not needed for normal use. The resolved path
is printed before the file is saved.

```{r locate-data-folder}
data_override <- if (exists("params")) params$data_dir else NULL
if (is.null(data_override)) {
  report_input <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
  project_dir <- if (length(report_input) == 1L && nzchar(report_input)) {
    dirname(normalizePath(report_input, mustWork = TRUE))
  } else getwd()
  repeat {
    candidate <- file.path(project_dir, "chapters", "07-thoroughness", "data")
    if (file.exists(file.path(project_dir, "_quarto.yml")) && dir.exists(candidate)) break
    parent_dir <- dirname(project_dir)
    if (identical(parent_dir, project_dir)) stop("Open the OER_r project, then rerun this chunk.")
    project_dir <- parent_dir
  }
  data_dir <- normalizePath(candidate, mustWork = TRUE)
} else {
  data_dir <- normalizePath(data_override, mustWork = TRUE)
}
stopifnot(dir.exists(data_dir))
output_file <- file.path(data_dir, "Science_Values.rds")
output_file
```

`saveRDS()` saves the one plain character vector. Rerunning this chunk replaces
the file at the displayed path. Students can keep the chapter's existing import
command, `Science_Values <- readRDS("Science_Values.rds")`. This is an RDS file,
not a saved workspace containing multiple objects.

```{r save-data-file}
saveRDS(Science_Values, file = output_file)
```

Read the file back from disk and compare it with the vector in memory. This
confirms that the saved object has the intended type, has no extra attributes,
contains every prepared passage, and can be read using the chapter's approach.

```{r verify-saved-data-file}
saved_text <- readRDS(output_file)
stopifnot(
  identical(saved_text, Science_Values),
  is.character(saved_text), is.null(attributes(saved_text)),
  all(!is.na(saved_text) & nzchar(trimws(saved_text)))
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  file = output_file,
  passages = length(saved_text),
  bytes = unname(file.info(output_file)$size),
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(output_file))
), caption = "Saved data file verified by reopening it")
```

## Completed output and remaining editorial work

The saved `Science_Values.rds` contains the Peels and colleagues text as a plain
character vector of natural passages. Identification, citation, source URL,
copyright, license, preparation information, notes, and references travel with
the text. Headings and list numbering are preserved in the passages.

`Science_Values_web`, `Science_Values_links`, and `passage_map` are available
while the report code runs, and can be recreated by rerunning it to trace
passages back to the source. The HTML shows selected review tables, not the
complete maps. These structures are not extra objects or attributes in the
student download. The report shows the extraction checks, passage composition,
search results, and saved-file verification so this preparation can be reviewed
and repeated.

The OER editor still needs to update Chapter 17's source identification and
citation, use consistent language for matching passages, and check its example
keywords against the results above. In particular, exact whole-word searches
for `bias` or `reproducibility` should not be assumed to produce a match.

The report can be knitted independently for review. Its rendered HTML should be
kept out of the published book output unless its publication is separately
requested. No code here edits the chapter, renders the book, or publishes it.
